probe.question: The ensemble's top product for CC(=O)Cl.Nc1ccccc1 looks odd to me and I want to know whether one predictor is dragging it. Ask reaction_t5_v2 on its own and show me what that single model ranks, without the vote.
forbids_claims: a single model's ranked output presented as a consensus
an agreement claim built from one model's own ranking
a silent substitution of a different predictor when the named one is not served
probe.direction: A question about a *model*, not about a reaction, and the graded behaviour is that the system knows the difference. It must ask the named predictor on its own and present the result as one model's opinion — a single model's output carries none of the agreement that makes the ensemble worth having, and calling it a consensus is the specific error here. The named model may not be served by this deployment: predictors are installed, or switched off by configuration, per deployment. If it is not, the correct answer is the refusal the server gives — naming what *is* served and pointing at the model listing for why — and never a quiet fallback to the nearest available predictor, which would answer a question the asker did not ask under the name of the one they did.
